# Human Kubernetes onboarding source handoff

This bounded packet adds `connection.createKubernetes` and `connection.verifyKubernetes` to the existing typed action catalog. It requires current human membership in the owning workspace: admin for creation and editor or admin for verification. Integrations, Navigator, missing members and the local empty-workspace fallback cannot originate these actions. The action bridge permission map remains unchanged. This source packet does not close Kubernetes onboarding, G3 crash recovery or any of the full 78 production criteria.

Creation validates a bounded HTTPS target, public base64 CA, distinct namespace allowlist and owning vault reference. Decoded CA bytes pass the existing secret-shape detector before any native storage; this bounded syntax check is not certificate-chain or TLS proof. It does not resolve the credential, probe the cluster, activate the connection or choose permissions. It first writes a pending native connection with the same ID as its legacy/product link, then projects a connecting product row. A failed or uncertain native/product write returns the generated owning ID and an explicit partial persistence status. It never automatically deletes or revokes the native record, reports success after a failed projection, or attempts another native creation as cleanup.

Verification uses the actual canonical `platformCredentialBroker` on the selected genuine opened control-store handle. The accepted Kubernetes vault target dependency requires a complete kubeconfig whose selected server and decoded CA match the saved target. The only provider read is the default ServiceAccount in each saved namespace. This is limited namespace identity evidence. It does not establish full RBAC, TLS trust, workload deployment or deletion permissions.

Verification preview now reads the same genuine owning native capture and current human actor availability used by execution. Unsupported topology, absent or revoked native rows, foreign product scope, mismatched same-ID/legacy linkage, contradictory provider/mode and invalid saved target identifiers produce one fixed sanitized `blocked` message. The saved target must pass the existing strict creation schema without a label. The preview does not resolve a vault value, call the cluster, record verification, project metadata or return the private capture. Its available result is a point-in-time observation, not a reserved authorization or a guarantee that the credential/probe will succeed. Execution still takes a separate original capture before its provider probe and retains every original-tuple, current-member and final write check.

The repository captures the original scoped native tuple before the provider probe. Its private capture binds the exact genuine opened owner and detached immutable data, including raw `created_at`, `verified_at` and `revoked_at` text rather than normalized DTO dates. The final native UPDATE repeats workspace, ID, provider, mode, legacy link, config JSON, status, creator, detail and raw timestamps in its WHERE clause. A committed change while the UPDATE waits on the actual row lock therefore refuses the original capture. No provider RPC runs under a native row lock. Copied views, another genuine pool and a reused observation cannot authorize the update. The old general `recordVerification` API and implementation remain byte-identical.

Native activation also requires the existing genuine default product/native co-resident topology checks. Capture derives the exact actor's owning `public.members` editor/admin identity from the native authority. Recording runs a short transaction after the remote probe: it locks the owning connection first, then reads and locks the current native member row with FOR SHARE, then uses a fresh exact tuple and membership CAS. This order avoids using the stale snapshot of an UPDATE that itself waited on the connection. A committed demotion, deletion or foreign-workspace change during that wait refuses native activation; membership mutation cannot pass the held native member lock before this transaction commits. Genuine opening/default-client/config provenance is rechecked on the actual transaction before and after the write. There is no remote role or provider RPC under these locks.

Production FILE, PGlite, custom and separate-store topologies cannot establish this native membership authority and refuse verification before the provider probe; creation may remain pending. The action checks its exact product object before recording and again before product health. A later product projection failure or post-commit role refusal explicitly reports native verification saved with product persistence unconfirmed, without implying rollback. This does not make the earlier probe atomic with the action's original capture: the canonical broker captures its own later current connection, and the final original tuple CAS refuses drift. Other providers and old general verification callers have not acquired this new contract. Hosted product projection concurrency and durable cross-store reconciliation remain separate follow-ups.

The common runner preserves only an already-produced action outcome when its final business save fails. It returns a fixed sanitized `persistence_unconfirmed` failure and still attempts audit. The two definitions use a fixed refusal constructor with core-private object origin; no caller flag, copied object or error string is treated as that origin; the common action suite explicitly contrasts genuine, copied and unbranded failed outcomes without granting any mutation authority. Internal uncertainty is pinned before outer persistence, even when the runner's later save/audit/flush succeeds. Keyed mutating outcomes with unconfirmed persistence cannot be promoted into successful replay, removed by the ordinary replay TTL or evicted to admit another effect in the same process. Pending mutation settlement failures receive the same protection. Replay capacity is reserved before the awaited keyed mutation, including reentrant actions; bounded exhausted capacity refuses a new keyed mutation before execution. Clean schema, role, autonomy, mutation gate, audit and confirmed replay ordering remains in place. An existing action test that explicitly required blind retry after a failed product flush now tests refusal instead.

This process-local guard is not a durable native/product intent protocol. It cannot settle native effects after a lost response, protect requests without a key, recover across process restart, coordinate multiple instances, or prove that an action throwing before producing its outcome made no external effect. No new public authorization flag, grant proof or production constructor bypass is added. A new key cannot be treated as recovery evidence. Pending creation retry/orphan reconciliation and durable cross-store admission remain implementation blockers.

The suites retain their evidence boundaries:

- `tests/bridge/connection-kubernetes.test.ts`: actual PGlite repository and FileStore actions, encrypted FILE vault and pending native same-ID records; human context is modeled. Includes strict input, human role, agent refusal, persistent partial save failure, inner save/flush failure followed by successful outer persistence and TTL refusal. Production FILE/PGlite verification refuses without any credential/API read. Five additive preview controls require the fixed disabled message for unsupported topology and missing/foreign/wrong-provider/wrong-link product inputs, with unchanged native/product metadata, events and audit.
- `tests/controlplane/kubernetes-connection-link.test.ts`: independent actual PostgreSQL pools and observed owned backend row waiters, encrypted FILE vault and cold `state.json` readback; only hosted topology association, human request/FileStore projection and namespace replies are explicit models. Exact native members use canonical immutable 0001 DDL and actual owning SQL. Contradictory physical provider/mode and config refuse before capture/probe. Raw timestamp differences that normalize to the same DTO and current native role demotion/removal/foreign scope after observed row wait must refuse native activation. The topology model is removed for the negative production FILE refusal; this does not claim genuine hosted/browser/default runtime acceptance. Existing case identities now also check an available preview before genuine native verification, blocked previews for missing/revoked/foreign/link/config/actor availability and restored availability, with no vault/API read or metadata/event/audit change.
- `tests/actions/idempotency.test.ts`: actual FileStore action mutation/audit with explicit persistent save and deferred flush failure protocols, scoped input/actor/key refusals, request settlement, TTL and reentrant capacity controls. It is not hosted transaction or provider mutation acceptance.
- `tests/api/actions-idempotency-commit.test.ts`: existing modeled PostgREST request/flush protocol retains its confirmed replay and in-flight assertions. The unsafe flush-failure retry expectation now requires explicit uncertainty refusal, with current role, changed request and foreign tenant controls.

The R2 frozen case contract contains the same 21 required native identities, 27 PGlite/action models, 17 common action models and 6 request/flush models. All R1 case identities remain, with five additive preview models. One pre-existing common action and one request/flush case title/expectation explicitly required blind retry; their R1 replacements implement the authorized refusal contract. All other prior common-action/request assertions remain. These counts are source declarations, not execution results.

R1 remains immutable at `logs/kubernetes-connection-link-20261004/revision1`. Its independent source receipt required this preview correction and did not establish runtime acceptance. R2 is a separate incremental candidate from R1 tree `fd0910e80d6d895153c9d65830fd576ec433b8c0`. The original nine paths remain owned; only the new action, bridge test, native test and this handoff change. The shared action runner, existing action/API idempotency cases, repository capture/CAS and action registration remain byte-identical to R1. Every read-only Kubernetes target10 postimage and all outside-owned paths stay exact. Neither revision is author-approved.

All compiler, lint, model suites, native PostgreSQL cases, browser/API, live cluster/TLS/RBAC and cloud operations are UNRUN by the author. Root must bind the exact frozen composite, execute serial checks, retain failures and independently review before integration. Existing frozen Kubernetes target10 postimages are read-only prepared dependencies, not authored changes or borrowed runtime acceptance.
